card.name: Khaleegy (Khaliji)
card.era: Traditional; music traced to Umayyad/Islamic period
card.tagline: Gulf women's hair-and-thobe dance swaying to khaleeji rhythms
card.profile: Khaleegy is a women's social folk dance of the Arabian Gulf - Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, the UAE, Qatar and Oman - performed in groups at weddings, engagements and holidays (Wikipedia). It is danced in a loose, richly embroidered overdress called the thobe al-nashal worn without a hip belt, emphasizing gliding footwork, shoulder shimmies, hand gestures and the rhythmic side-to-side tossing of long, unbound hair to khaleeji rhythms (Belly Dance Geek). The floating dress and hair are often linked to the region's maritime, pearl-diving and Bedouin heritage.
card.insight: Known in the UAE as raks al-nashal and in Kuwait as samri, it was traditionally danced privately in women-only gatherings; by the early 1980s famous Egyptian belly dancers including Sohair Zaki and Nagwa Fouad began incorporating stylized Khaleeji phrases into their stage shows (Suhaila International).
card.image_significance: The Gulf hair-toss dance. A representative image shows a line or row formation, often with canes, swords or flowing veils — Arabian Gulf, Gulf states.
